paper.title: Tiltrotor CFD Part II: aerodynamic optimisation of tiltrotor blades

assumptions.title: Tiltrotor blade design is a two-regime compromise problem
assumptions.summary: Hover and airplane modes impose conflicting aerodynamic requirements, especially in blade twist and tip behavior.

assumptions.title: Publicly reproducible geometry is sufficient for an open approximation
assumptions.summary: The public XV-15 radius, chord, cutout, twist relation at r/R=0.75, and airfoil family are enough to reconstruct a low-order baseline.

assumptions.title: The paper's exact HMB3 plus discrete-adjoint stack is not public
assumptions.summary: The open reproduction must preserve the objective structure and variables while approximating the flow model.

methods.title: Ten-variable blade parameterization
methods.summary: Seven Bernstein twist variables, two chord variables, and one sweep variable.

methods.title: Trim-at-fixed-thrust evaluation
methods.summary: Every candidate design is compared at the baseline thrust coefficient for the selected operating condition.

methods.title: Single-point and weighted multi-point optimization
methods.summary: Single-point cases optimize one regime; multi-point cases optimize a weighted sum across hover and airplane modes.

experiments.title: Hover single-point cases HM1 HM2 HM3
Weighted multi-point cases MP1 MP2 MP3

claims.title: Twist-only optimization improves hover FoM
support: HM1 and HM2 both beat the baseline in hover.

claims.title: Twist-only optimization improves airplane efficiency more strongly than hover FoM
support: AM1 improves eta by 6.593% versus HM2 improving FoM by 1.988%.

claims.title: Chord and sweep matter more in airplane mode than in hover
support: HM2 to HM3 adds little hover gain.
AM1 to AM2 adds a materially larger eta gain.

claims.title: Multi-point optimization yields compromise blades
support: MP cases retain some hover benefit while recovering part of the airplane gain.

claims.title: The best compromise in the paper is MP3
support: MP3 gives the largest eta increase among multi-point cases with only a small hover penalty.

claims.title: Adjoint-based optimization was evaluation-efficient in the original paper
support: This claim belongs to the original HMB3 workflow and is recorded but not directly reproduced by the open model.

extension.title: Dense weight sweep of the hover/airplane trade-off
extension.summary: Use vectorized batched evaluation to extend the reported three multi-point cases into a denser Pareto-style map.

extension.title: CUDA-X acceleration for batched multi-point design sweeps
extension.summary: Use CuPy when available to accelerate weight and sweep-parameter sweeps without changing the model assumptions.
